prompt: When tracing is started with page snapshots turned on, Playwright calls on a page whose main thread is busy never finish, and even an explicit timeout on the call does not fire. Repro: start a local HTTP server, launch Chromium, create a context, start tracing with snapshots on, open a page and navigate to the server. Evaluate a script in the page that schedules an endless loop to start right after the script returns. Then navigate again with a 3-second timeout. With snapshots off, the evaluation returns at once and the navigation fails with a timeout error after about 3 seconds. With snapshots on, both calls stay pending (checked for 20 seconds; in CI a navigation with a 30-second timeout hung for more than 3 days). It happens every time on macOS and Linux, and also through the Python binding. Expected: tracing must not turn a bounded call into an unbounded one. Reporter's analysis: the steps that run before and after each call have a 3-second budget, but that budget can only cut off waits that are tied to it. The DOM snapshot capture waits on the page directly, so when the page never answers, the call never gets a response. A lint check meant to catch such untied waits misses this spot because the call uses optional chaining. Tying the snapshot wait to the budget, as the coverage capture already does, makes the repro finish.
done_when_reason: The new test navigates with a 1-second timeout on a page in an endless loop while tracing with snapshots, and expects the normal timeout error. Any fix that lets the timeout fire passes; the message is the standard one already shown in the issue.
concerns: The original issue gives the root cause and the exact patch. L1 keeps the analysis in plain words, which still points strongly at the snapshot code. The real fix also touches the lint plugin and a trace viewer file, which the tests do not need.

Attaching Playwright to an already running Chromium through the Chrome DevTools Protocol can give a page whose main frame is wrongly replaced by a deeply nested iframe. Page shape: a top document on 127.0.0.1 holds a cross-site iframe on localhost (out of process); that iframe holds a same-process child iframe, which holds a sandboxed iframe with inline srcdoc content (its own iframe target). Repro: serve these pages from a local HTTP server, start the bundled Chromium headless with remote debugging on and the top URL open, wait until all frames load, then connect Playwright and take that page. Expected: evaluation on the page runs in the top-level document: the location is the top URL, the window is its own top window, and a locator finds the heading of the top document. Actual: evaluation throws an error that the execution context was destroyed by a navigation, although nothing navigates. With another Chrome version, evaluation runs inside the sandboxed srcdoc frame, the frame list shows only the top URL, the heading is not found, and keyboard input does not reach the top document. It first appeared on a real site with ads in nested sandboxed frames. Reporter's analysis: the nested out-of-process frame is reported with a parent frame that Playwright never registered, so it is attached as if it had no parent, and that path gives the main frame the iframe's identity. Skipping such frames keeps the main frame but leaves the nested frames missing. Seen in 1.63 and 1.60.

Also, when an existing same-process child frame is navigated to a cross-site page (so it moves to its own process), it stays the same frame object: the navigation response belongs to that frame, the frame and its evaluated location show the new URL, the page fires exactly one frame-navigated event (with the new URL), and the page still has two frames.

prompt: Playwright's API request context stores a cookie as already expired when its Set-Cookie header has Max-Age first and then an Expires date in the past. Example: a server sets a session id cookie with Max-Age of one hour, followed by Expires set to 1 January 1970 and path /. A later request does not send the cookie, so a server that echoes the cookie header gets an empty value. With the same two attributes in the other order, the cookie is kept. Expected: Max-Age takes precedence over Expires whatever the order of the attributes (RFC 6265 section 5.3), as in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, so the cookie lives one hour and is sent. Servers often send a past Expires next to Max-Age for old clients. Cause: the attributes are read in order and both set the same expiry, so the last one wins. A related problem: a Max-Age value that is not an optional minus sign followed only by digits (for example "10abc", or an empty value) is still read as a number; RFC 6265 section 5.2.2 says to ignore such an attribute. Seen on the main branch toward 1.64 and in 1.63; not platform-specific.
done_when_reason: The first new test checks Max-Age precedence in both orders, with positive and negative values; this follows from the issue. The second checks that non-numeric Max-Age values are ignored and the cookie stays a session cookie; the issue states this rule, and both levels keep it.
concerns: The non-numeric Max-Age part is a side note in the issue but has its own hidden test, so L1 and L2 both keep it.

prompt: Listing cookies for given URLs returns cookies that would not be sent to those URLs, and a cookie with path /foo/ is sent to /foo. Case 1: an API request context starts with a stored host-only cookie (domain example.com without a leading dot, path /api). Listing cookies for https://example.com/api/x returns it, which is right, but listing for https://sub.example.com/api/x and for https://example.com/apiv2 also returns it. Case 2: a server sets a cookie with path /foo/ on a response to /foo/set; a later request to /foo sends it. Expected, per the domain-match and path-match rules of RFC 6265 sections 5.1.3 and 5.1.4, which browsers follow and which the docs promise for browser contexts: a host-only cookie for example.com does not apply to sub.example.com, path /api does not apply to /apiv2, and path /foo/ does not apply to /foo. A path matches only exactly or on a slash boundary. Cause: the URL filter used for listing puts a dot in front of every cookie domain, so host-only cookies match all subdomains, and it compares paths as plain string prefixes. The API request context started to use this filter recently; before, it used the stricter check that decides what is sent. The same filter also serves cookie listing for browser contexts in all browsers, which report host-only cookies without a leading dot, so the bug likely exists there too. Separately, the path check used for sending adds a slash to the request path before it compares, so /foo matches /foo/. Seen on main toward 1.64 and in 1.63.
done_when_reason: The new tests check cookie listing for browser contexts and API request contexts, and cookie sending, with host-only, domain and slash-path cookies. The issue states all these rules and says browser contexts are affected too, so a full fix passes. One old test now marks a cookie as domain-wide, which matches the new rules.

Since pandas 3.0, selecting one row together with a list of columns that are not next to each other returns a small Series that keeps a large temporary array alive. Example: a DataFrame with 100,000 rows and four float columns; select row 0 and three of the four columns by label. The result has three values, but its data is a view into a 3 by 100,000 array. That array is a temporary copy made while the columns are selected, not the DataFrame's own data. Each result keeps about 2.3 MB alive for 24 bytes of data, and the cost grows with the number of rows. Collecting 100 such results in a list uses about 229 MiB. The same happens with selection by position, and when the columns are selected first and the row after. Selecting the row first and then the columns does not have the problem. In pandas 2.3.3 the result owned its data, or with copy-on-write turned on was backed only by its three values, and there was no memory growth. The problem is present from 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 and on the main branch. The small result should not keep the temporary alive.
Done when: the result also does not keep the temporary alive when a slice of rows is selected together with a list of columns, by label or by position; selections that are views of the DataFrame's own data, such as a row slice of one column or one row with a slice of columns, stay views and are not copied.
done_when: Done when: the result also does not keep the temporary alive when a slice of rows is selected together with a list of columns, by label or by position; selections that are views of the DataFrame's own data, such as a row slice of one column or one row with a slice of columns, stay views and are not copied.
done_when_reason: Tests also cover a row slice with a list of columns (loc and iloc), which the issue does not mention, and a second test asserts that views of the DataFrame's own data stay views; a fix that copies every such result would fail it.
